1.reproduce_code:
---
title: "Figure Rendering Test"
format: html
---

```{r}
#| fig-cap: !expr caption
caption = character(0)
knitr::include_graphics("http://arfer.net/mlp/img/rara-jiggs.png")
```
1.explanation: To reproduce the bug, create a Quarto document with an R code block that includes a `fig-cap` option. Set the `fig-cap` to evaluate to `character(0)`, which is a zero-length character vector. This will cause the figure not to render when the document is rendered to HTML using Quarto. The provided code snippet demonstrates this setup.
1.bug_scenario: The bug occurs when the `fig-cap` option in an R code block evaluates to `character(0)`, causing the figure not to render in the output document. This is demonstrated by changing `caption = "hello world"` to `caption = character(0)` in the Quarto document, which results in the image not being displayed.
